registryLegalName: Sealing of Records After an Unconditional Pardon (NRS 179.273)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Sealing of records after unconditional pardon: Automatic sealing; petition; no fee. The section is described by the controlling review as providing automatic sealing together with a no-fee petition route for the case where the automatic sealing has not happened.

verificationStatute.description: No verification or notarization statute is identified for NRS 179.273, and the no-fee petition's required contents are unread. Nothing is filled.

presentation.verificationPenaltyLabel: the penalties for a false statement

counselFlags: Record sealing, never expungement. The Nevada Department of Public Safety states directly that sealing is not expungement because it does not authorise destruction of the records.
Sealing does not restore firearm rights. Only a pardon that does not restrict the right to bear arms does.
Nevada orders do not bind out-of-state agencies and do not reach federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records.
Waiting period: none. The section provides automatic sealing on an unconditional pardon, with a no-fee petition available where the automatic sealing has not occurred.

Fee: the chapter-index title records the NRS 179.273 petition as carrying no fee. That characterisation comes from the index heading alone, because the section text is unread; confirm before relying on it.
No verification or notarization statute is identified for NRS 179.273, and the no-fee petition's required contents are unread. Nothing is filled.

Verification before filing: because sealing is automatic in the first instance, the first step is to verify whether the record has already been sealed, not to file. How a person verifies this is part of the unread statutory text.

Scope: a conditional pardon, or any pardon short of an unconditional one, is not reached by the section. Anyone who does not yet hold a pardon is out of scope — applying for one is a Nevada Board of Pardons matter.

registryExcerpt.venue: The court in which the conviction was entered, for the petition route. No venue applies to the automatic route.
registryExcerpt.destinationName: The district attorney's or city attorney's office first, then the clerk of the appropriate court

waitingPeriods.duration: none. The section provides automatic sealing, with a no-fee petition available where it has not occurred

exclusions: A conditional pardon, or any pardon short of an unconditional one, which the section does not reach.
Anyone who does not yet hold a pardon. Applying for one is a Board of Pardons matter and is out of scope.
